no11.summary: Lebel reports to Charles Emmanuel I that Mayenne is again thinking of claiming the crown, encouraged by letters from Rome; the Pope and the King of Spain want a Catholic king elected, Mayenne will favour whichever candidate brings him most advantage, and his secret council is the archbishop of Lyon (Épinac), Villeroy and président Jeannin.
no11.en:
I shall only tell you by this letter that I have learned, and from a good quarter, that the Duke of Mayenne is
from day to day coming back to the opinion of [?claiming] the [?crown] for himself, principally because of this fancy
[given him] by letters from Rome, in which he is written that the Pope said it would be very ill [?gone], if, being
able to [?have] the crown for himself, he gave it to another. Your Highness sees well what likelihood there is that
this second(?) design, or to put it better, leave, can take effect.

no62.summary: Mayenne's discontent has been bought off with 40,000 écus down and assignations up to 260,000 écus; Feria brings a doctor who wants to dispute the crown on points of law, which is openly mocked; the Spanish army is smaller than any before it, those around Mayenne will propose a truce, and Lebel advises courting Mayenne.
no62.en:
I have learned since my last that the discontent which the Duke of Mayenne had with Monsieur has been remedied, he
having had satisfaction given him for what was owed to him, and the sum was larger than I wrote before; they have
[?offered] him forty thousand écus and had assignations given him, both in [?Flanders] and in Spain, up to the cash
amount of two hundred and sixty thousand écus. It was thought that, after so many remonstrances made to the
[?servants] of the King of Spain about the impossibility of his pretensions to this [crown?] … the [?kingdom] be for
[?him], the Infanta and the prince, that he would have resolved to have some other of his kin attain it;

no100.summary: If Philip II's designs for the Infanta fail, Savoy could with more reason than any other prince hope for the crown from the Estates; money for his 'compagnon' and président Jeannin, paid through Zamet, Feria's and Commandeur Tassis's letters, good offices with the Pope, the Provence governorship, Vaudemont and the château of Miolans. With nos. 11 and 62 it follows Savoy's candidacy at the Estates of the League, January to March 1593.
no100.en:
On the 13th of this month I wrote to Your Highness, and I am still awaiting with good devotion Your Highness's
commands, having received none since my departure, and even to hear that mine of the 25th of last month arrived
safely, in which I repeated to you the principal points of what was contained in my letters of the 5th and 15th of
January, which I believe were held up at Nevers. And in which I also told you that the lord has not made the credit
over here that he wanted people to believe. He is very short of means. He has, in truth, lords and [?friends] among
them.

snip.cap: Fr. 3983 no. 62, f. 130r (10 March 1593): the clear opening, then the cipher, letter signs run together and code numbers set off by dots
snip.credit: Bibliothèque nationale de France, fr. 3983 f. 130r, via Gallica btv1b9059406b

system: Homophonic substitution (1-2 signs per letter), three nulls, an et sign, and a ~300-number code set off by dots with an alphabetical addendum above 300; key published by Tomokiyo.
